name: CapBencher
description: Publishing a large language model (LLM) benchmark (especially its ground-truth answers) on the Internet risks contaminating future LLMs and enabling evaluation gaming: it may be unintentionally (or intentionally) used to train or select a model, or exploited to overfit and hack leaderboards when labels are accessible. A common mitigation is to keep the benchmark private and let participants submit their models or predictions to the organizers, but this still permits test-set overfitting through feedback loops.
